summary: B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact Upload signature, preserves FilesOption, and directly reuses multipartbody.NewFile. A changes the required API and adds explicitly prohibited association machinery.
reasons: B implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly; A instead accepts ...FilesUploadOption.

B keeps the established FilesOption query and request-option handling intact. A introduces FilesUploadOption, seven association options, multipart fields, and changes WithFilesRequestOptions, contrary to the explicit scope restrictions.
B uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile exactly as required. A expands the helper with duplicate NewFileWithFields machinery for out-of-scope associations.

Neither patch routes Upload through FilesService.Add as required; both duplicate Add's request, decoding, and error logic. This is B's main contract violation, but A has the same violation plus several more severe API and scope violations beyond it all existing behavior machinery changes both carry risk but B's API surface remains much closer to required contract.
risks_a: Public Upload signature violates the exact required API.
Adds association fields and options explicitly forbidden by the contract.

Changes existing option types and broadens multipart helper functionality unnecessarily not needed for task scope and may affect compatibility expectations despite gates passing it still creates maintenance burden (larger surface area). Including raw retry refactor also outside requested scope.
risks_b: Upload duplicates Add instead of delegating to it, risking future drift in validation, request construction, decoding, and error semantics.
No visible test covers propagation of a source-reader failure; retry coverage uses replay-friendly strings.Reader rather than an explicitly one-shot streamed source.

The RawClient seekable-body refactor is outside the requested focused implementation. Its silent failure paths can leave a reader displaced at EOF if seeking to the end succeeds but restoring the original offset fails.
